newsitem.title: CHINA: McDonald's to shut disputed China store.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's to shut disputed China store.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. will close its flagship restaurant in the heart of Beijing to make way for a shopping plaza after holding out for two years against a removal order, a spokeswoman said Sunday.

The restaurant, at one end of Beijing's Wangfujing shopping street and just off central Tiananmen Square, will close on Monday and be demolished, Zhang Ziyun, spokesman for Beijing McDonald's Food Co. Ltd., said.

McDonald's has agreed to move the restaurant, its first in Beijing and one of the largest in the world, to make way for a huge commercial and shopping complex to be built by Hong Kong's Cheung Kong (Holdings), Zhang said in an interview.
"In order to coordinate with the construction of the plaza we are closing down and moving," she said.
McDonald's had apparently resisted the move on the grounds that it had signed a 20-year lease on the site on prime land in the centre of the capital.
But the company has reached an agreement with Beijing authorities to relocate the flagship restaurant about 150 yards further north on Wangfujing shopping street, Zhang said.
"We held talks with the relevant departments of the Beijing city government and both sides feel very satisfied," she said.
The fast-food chain will receive compensation for the move and also plans to open at least two more outlets along the shopping street, Zhang added.
The company has 26 restaurants in Beijing and plans to open three more by year-end. It has more than 100 restaurants in 15 cities in China.
